Q: failed to find Build Tools revision 21.1.1 - sdk up to date A:

In the error window where it displays message as failed to find build tools versions, it also gives the link to install the tools version. You can update using that.

If the above option is not available then another way is: Open the sdk tools tab from sdk manager in android studio. Click on 'Launch StandAlone SDK Manager'. In the new window, you will be able to see all the revisions of build tools, api levels, system images. From there you can select the tools revision which are missing and install.

Q: Why is numpy's sine function so inaccurate at some points? A:

my_wave = np.sin(np.arange(0, length, length / resolution))

The set of numbers supplied by np.arrange are correct increment x+=0.06283185

[using sin(arrange) with Excel as expected ] https://i.sstatic.net/BS6GC.png

[Using np.sin(arrange) with numpy very wrong] https://i.sstatic.net/l6qnZ.png

Using math.sin with the same set of numbers is also good. Using np.sin with the same set of numbers is also good.

The problem is calling np.sin with a pointer to the array my_wave = np.sin(np.arange(0, length, length / resolution)) isn't good

However np.arrange is also good

Q: What Udemy Self Learning Courses Do You Suggest? A:

Honestly, Dr. Angela Yu’s course is already a very good starting point. Since you’re beginning from zero, the most important thing right now is building a strong foundation rather than trying to learn everything at once. I’d focus on finishing that course fully and using it to get comfortable with how Python works and how coding logic feels.

For the kind of things you want to build — gaming trackers, APIs, and Excel/database tools — Python is honestly one of the best choices. Once you’re comfortable with the basics, you can slowly move into learning APIs, databases, and Excel automation with Python. AI tools like ChatGPT also become incredibly useful once you understand the fundamentals, because they can help you build projects faster and explain things when you get stuck.

The biggest thing I’d recommend is not jumping between too many courses early on. Most beginners get stuck in tutorial mode. Small personal projects will teach you far more than endlessly watching videos. Even something simple like a gaming tracker that stores player stats in Excel or a database would already teach you a huge amount.
